id: p:French Mandate for Syria and Lebanon
name: French Mandate for Syria and Lebanon
The Americas before 1492
text: Long before the first Europeans crossed the Atlantic Ocean, hundreds of Native nations lived in the Americas. They had many different languages, governments, ways of farming and beliefs. This map shows only a few of them, because its data has borders for only a few.

name: European exploration and colonies
text: Christopher Columbus arrived in the Americas, and European countries began to take land there for colonies. Contact with Europeans started epidemics that killed millions of Native Americans. Europeans enslaved Native Americans, and they also brought enslaved Africans to the Americas.

name: American Revolution
text: On July 4, 1776, the Continental Congress adopted the Declaration of Independence. In it, thirteen British colonies in North America said that they were now free and independent states, with no ties to the British king.

name: The Constitution
text: In the summer of 1787, delegates met in Philadelphia and wrote the Constitution. This document of four pages, signed on September 17, 1787, set up the government of the United States.

name: War of 1812
text: From 1812 to 1815 the United States and Great Britain were at war. On December 24, 1814, the two sides signed the Treaty of Ghent. It put the borders in North America back where they were before the war.

name: Westward expansion
text: In 1803 the United States bought 828,000 square miles of land west of the Mississippi River from France, for 15 million dollars. This made the country twice as large. As more Americans moved west, there was conflict with the Native Americans who lived on that land.

name: Reform movements and women's rights
text: On July 19 and 20, 1848, the first Women's Rights Convention met at Seneca Falls, New York. At the end, 68 women and 32 men signed the Declaration of Sentiments, which Elizabeth Cady Stanton helped to write.

name: Slavery and the Civil War
text: The Civil War lasted from 1861 to 1865. Eleven southern states, the Confederacy, fought the Union of the other states. In the Confederacy lived 5.5 million free people and 3.5 million enslaved people. Another 500,000 people were enslaved in the border states.

name: The end of slavery: the 13th Amendment
text: The 13th Amendment to the Constitution abolished slavery in the United States. Congress passed it on January 31, 1865, and the states ratified it on December 6, 1865.

name: Reconstruction
text: Reconstruction, from 1865 to 1877, was the time after the Civil War. New laws and amendments to the Constitution changed what it means to be an American citizen. With the 14th Amendment, the national government had to guarantee that all Americans are equal before the law, regardless of race.

name: Immigration and Ellis Island
text: From 1892 to 1924, Ellis Island in New York Harbor was the largest immigration station of the United States. More than 12 million immigrants passed through it.

name: Expansion overseas
text: In 1898 the United States won a war against Spain. In the peace treaty, Spain gave up its claim to Cuba, and it handed Guam, Puerto Rico and the Philippines over to the United States. The United States paid 20 million dollars for the Philippines. During the war it also took Hawaii.

name: Great Depression
text: The Great Depression was a very bad time for business and work in the whole world. People in the United States link it with the fall of the stock market on October 24, 1929. In 1933 about one worker in four, 12,830,000 people, had no job. President Franklin D. Roosevelt then started the New Deal, a program to bring the economy back.

name: Civil rights movement
text: President Lyndon Johnson signed the Civil Rights Act on July 2, 1964. The law made discrimination in public places and in jobs illegal, and it called for schools to be open to all races. It was the widest civil rights law since Reconstruction.

name: River valley civilizations
text: The first cities grew thousands of years ago where the soil was rich. Among them were Eridu, Uruk and Ur in Mesopotamia, between the Euphrates and Tigris rivers in today's Iraq. Cities also grew beside the Nile in Egypt and Sudan, in the Indus River valley, and beside the Huang He, or Yellow River, in China.

name: World religions begin
text: Buddhism has its roots in Nepal and India, in the late 500s BCE. Traders and missionaries carried it along the trade routes to other parts of Asia. Judaism, Christianity and Islam all trace their beginnings to Abraham. The Levant, at the east end of the Mediterranean Sea, is important to all three, and some call it the Holy Land.

name: The Roman Empire
text: The Roman Empire began in 27 BCE. At its largest, in 117 CE, Rome ruled land from western Europe to the Middle East. In 476 CE the western half of the empire fell. The eastern half went on, as the Byzantine Empire, until 1453.

name: The Silk Road
text: The Silk Road was not one road. It was a network of routes that traders used for more than 1,500 years, from 130 BCE, when the Han dynasty of China opened trade, to 1453 CE. Traders carried silk from China to Europe, and ideas moved with the goods.

name: The Aztec Empire
text: In about a hundred years the Aztec built an empire in today's central Mexico. In 1428 their city Tenochtitlan joined with two other cities, Texcoco and Tlacopan, in the Triple Alliance. Spanish soldiers surrounded the capital in 1521, and it fell on August 13 of that year.

name: The Inca Empire
text: The Inca Empire, in the Andes mountains of South America, was once the largest civilization of the Americas. The Inca had no writing, so much of what is known was written down later by Spanish colonizers. Spanish soldiers led by Francisco Pizarro took the Inca ruler Atahualpa prisoner in a surprise attack, and later killed him.

name: The Han dynasty of China
text: The Han dynasty ruled China from 202 BCE to 220 CE, with a short break from 9 to 23 CE. People see it as a golden age of Chinese history. Paper was invented in this time, and the Han helped to open the Silk Road trade route. Most people of China today call themselves the Han people.

name: The Maya
text: The Maya lived in what is now southeastern Mexico, Guatemala, Belize and the west of Honduras and El Salvador. Their first cities grew around 750 BCE. They had the most developed writing of the Americas before Columbus, and many city-states, not one empire. The last Maya city fell to Spain in 1697. More than 6 million Maya live in nearly the same area today.

name: The Kingdom of Aksum
text: The kingdom of Aksum arose in the first century CE in the north of today's Ethiopia. It grew rich from trade routes that linked the Roman Empire with the Middle East and India, and it was the first African country to make its own coins. In the 300s it became Christian. It was strongest from the 200s to the 500s. Its power was gone by the end of the 700s.

name: The Byzantine Empire
text: The Byzantine Empire was the eastern part of the Roman Empire. The emperor Constantine I, who ruled from 324 to 337, founded its capital, Constantinople. The empire lived on after the western part fell in the 400s. It was largest under Justinian I, who ruled from 527 to 565. Its people called themselves Romans. The empire ended in 1453, when the Ottomans took Constantinople.

name: The spread of Islam
text: After the death of Muhammad in 632 CE, Muslim armies conquered large areas. Their states, the caliphates, came to hold land on three continents: Asia, Africa and Europe. Islam spread out from the city of Mecca towards the Indian, Atlantic and Pacific oceans. In some parts of the world, such as Indonesia, trade carried the religion.

name: The Great Schism of 1054
text: In 1054 the Christian church broke into two: the Catholic Church in the west and the Eastern Orthodox Church in the east. The two sides had long disagreed about beliefs, customs and the power of the pope. In 1204 crusaders from the west sacked the city of Constantinople. The split has never been healed. 1054 is the usual date, but some scholars give other dates.

name: Timbuktu
text: Timbuktu is a city near the Niger River in today's Mali, where the savanna meets the Sahara desert. Camel caravans with salt and other goods made it rich. From the 13th to the 16th centuries it was a centre of Islamic learning, with a university of 25,000 students and several hundred thousand manuscripts. In the 16th century invaders from Morocco began to drive the scholars out.

name: The Reformation
text: The Reformation was a movement in the western Christian church, in Europe in the 1500s. It challenged the pope and the Catholic Church, and Protestant churches began with it. It is usually dated from 1517, when Martin Luther published his Ninety-five Theses. The printing press helped to spread the new ideas fast. People do not agree on the year it ended. One date they give is 1648.

name: Ancient Egypt
text: Ancient Egypt was a civilization along the lower part of the Nile River, in the north-east of Africa. It began around 3150 BCE, when Upper and Lower Egypt were united. The floods of the Nile and irrigation gave rich harvests. Egypt was strongest in the time called the New Kingdom. One date given for its end is 30 BCE, when Rome conquered Egypt.

name: Mesopotamia
text: Mesopotamia is the land of the Tigris and Euphrates rivers, about where Iraq is today. Some of the first civilizations of the world grew there. The Sumerians and the Akkadians led the region from about 3100 BCE, when written history begins. Empires came from about 2350 BCE, with Sargon of Akkad. In 539 BCE Babylon fell, and the empire of Cyrus the Great conquered Mesopotamia.

name: Ancient Greece
text: Ancient Greece was not one country. It was several hundred city-states with the same language and culture, around the north-east of the Mediterranean Sea. The city-states began to form in the 8th century BCE. Athens and Sparta fought each other in the Peloponnesian War. Alexander the Great conquered the Persian empire and died in 323 BCE. His conquests spread Greek culture into Africa and Asia.

name: The Roman Republic
text: The Roman Republic began in 509 BCE, by the traditional date, when the Romans ended the rule of their kings. In its time Rome grew from a city and the land around it to the leading power of the whole Mediterranean world. There were elections each year, but a few powerful families held most of the high offices. The republic ended in 27 BCE, when the Roman Empire began.

name: The Qin dynasty of China
text: The Qin dynasty was the first imperial dynasty of China. By 221 BCE the state of Qin had conquered its rival states and united China, and its king became the first emperor, Qin Shi Huang. The Qin made money, weights, measures and writing the same in the whole country, and joined walls in the north that later became the Great Wall. The dynasty fell in 206 BCE. The Han dynasty came next.

name: The Middle Ages in Europe
text: In the history of Europe, the Middle Ages lasted from about 500 to about 1500. They began with the fall of the western Roman Empire. New kingdoms grew on its land. In the system called feudalism, knights and lower nobles fought for their lords, and in return they got the rent from land. People do not agree on one end date; 1500 is often used.

name: The Crusades
text: The Crusades were wars that the popes called for between 1095 and 1291, against Muslim rulers, to win and hold the Holy Land. Pope Urban II called for the First Crusade in 1095, to take Jerusalem. After it, the crusaders set up four states in the Levant. Saladin, a Muslim ruler, destroyed their armies in 1187. The Third Crusade saved the states, but Jerusalem stayed under Muslim rule.

name: The Mongol Empire
text: The Mongol Empire was the largest empire of connected land in history. It began in 1206 in today's Mongolia, when Genghis Khan was named ruler of all Mongols. At its largest it reached from the Sea of Japan to eastern Europe. It linked the East and the West, so trade, tools and ideas moved across Asia and Europe. By 1294 it had split into four parts.

name: The Black Death
text: The Black Death was a plague that struck Europe from 1346 to 1353. It was one of the deadliest diseases in human history. Up to 50 million people died, about 30% to 60% of the people of Europe. A bacterium caused it, and flea bites spread it most of the time. Reports say that it came to Europe in 1347 through a trading port in Crimea, and that ships carried it on.

name: Trade across the Sahara
text: Trade across the Sahara desert linked North Africa with the rest of Africa. It was at its height from the 8th century to the early 17th century. Caravans of camels carried the goods. A usual caravan had about 1,000 camels, and some had 12,000. Guides who knew the desert led them. The city of Timbuktu became known across Europe for its wealth.

name: The Columbian Exchange
text: The Columbian Exchange was the movement of plants, animals and diseases between the Americas and Europe, Africa and Asia, after the voyage of Christopher Columbus in 1492. Maize, potatoes and tomatoes went out from the Americas. Rice, wheat, sugar cane and farm animals came in. Diseases from the Old World killed 80 to 95 percent of the Indigenous people of the Americas.

name: The Ottoman Empire
text: The Ottoman Empire began about 1299 as a small state in the north-west of today's Turkey, founded by Osman I. It grew to rule much of south-east Europe, west Asia and North Africa. In 1453 the Ottomans took Constantinople and ended the Byzantine Empire. Under Suleiman the Magnificent, in the 1500s, the empire became a world power. The rule of its sultans was ended in 1922.

name: The Ming dynasty of China
text: The Ming dynasty ruled China from 1368 to 1644, after the fall of the Yuan dynasty, which Mongols had led. The Yongle Emperor made Beijing a capital and built the Forbidden City. A man of his court, Zheng He, led seven very large sea voyages into the Indian Ocean, as far as Arabia and the east coast of Africa. Later the Ming joined and strengthened the Great Wall.

name: The Renaissance
text: The Renaissance was a time of great change in the art, building, writing, politics and technology of Europe. Its name means "rebirth". People found again the writing, ideas and art of the ancient Greeks and Romans. It began in the city of Florence, spread to the rest of Italy, and later to all of Europe. Most often it is dated to the 15th and 16th centuries; some date it from the 14th to the 17th.

name: The Songhai Empire
text: The Songhai Empire was a state in the west of the Sahel region of Africa, in the 15th and 16th centuries. At its largest it was one of the largest empires in the history of Africa. Its capital was Gao. It conquered the trading cities Timbuktu, in 1468, and Djenné, in 1475. The empire fell after it lost the Battle of Tondibi in 1591.

name: The Mughal Empire
text: The Mughal Empire ruled a large part of South Asia. By the usual account, Babur founded it in 1526, when he defeated the Sultan of Delhi. The empire was at its largest under Aurangzeb, its last major emperor. By 1760 it held only the region around Old Delhi. The British ended it after the Indian Rebellion of 1857.

name: The Scientific Revolution
text: The Scientific Revolution was a great change in how people in Europe studied nature, in the 16th and 17th centuries. The new science used more mathematics and looked for new evidence. It is often said to begin in 1543, with a book by Nicolaus Copernicus about the heavens and a book by Andreas Vesalius about the human body. It reached its high point in 1687, with a book by Isaac Newton.

name: Japan under the Tokugawa shoguns
text: From 1603 to 1868 the Tokugawa shoguns ruled Japan, with about 300 regional lords, the daimyo. This time is called the Edo period. It was a long time of peace, growing cities and strict social order. By 1639 Japan had sent away all foreigners except Dutch traders on one island at Nagasaki, and a period of isolation began.

name: The Enlightenment
text: The Enlightenment was a time of new ideas in Europe. It began in the late 17th century and was at its height in the 18th century. Its thinkers put weight on reason, evidence and the scientific method. They wrote about the freedom of each person, religious tolerance and natural rights, and they wanted government under a constitution. People give different years for its start and its end.

name: The Industrial Revolution
text: In the Industrial Revolution, people went from making things by hand to making them with machines in factories. Water and steam power came into wide use. It began in Great Britain around 1760 and had spread to the rest of Europe and to the United States by about 1840. Cloth making was the first industry to use the new methods. Output rose, and the population grew fast.

name: The French Revolution
text: The French Revolution changed the government and the society of France. It began in 1789 with a meeting of the Estates General. On 14 July 1789 the Bastille in Paris was stormed. The new National Assembly ended feudalism and wrote the Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen. The revolution ended in November 1799, when Napoleon Bonaparte came to power as First Consul.

name: The Haitian Revolution
text: In the French colony of Saint-Domingue, enslaved Africans rose against French rule on 21 August 1791. Toussaint Louverture, a former slave, became their best-known general. The colony became independent on 1 January 1804. Today it is Haiti. It is one of the only known slave revolts in history that led to a state free from slavery and ruled by people who had been enslaved.

name: Independence in Spanish America
text: In the early 19th century, wars across the Spanish Empire made new independent countries in the Americas. They began soon after France invaded Spain in 1808. From 1810, leaders such as Simón Bolívar and Agustín de Iturbide tried to build large new states. The fighting went on from 1809, in today's Bolivia, to 1829, in today's Mexico.

name: The Great Famine in Ireland
text: From 1845 to 1852 the people of Ireland suffered mass hunger and disease. A blight killed the potato crops, and the people depended on that one crop. Between 775,000 and 1.5 million people died, and a million or more left the country. Much food was sent out of Ireland in those years, and the government in London did not stop it. People argued about this then, and they still do.

name: The Taiping Rebellion
text: The Taiping Rebellion, from 1850 to 1864, was a civil war in China. The ruling Qing dynasty fought the rebels of the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom, and won. It was the deadliest civil war in history. Estimates of the dead start at 20 to 30 million people, and some are much higher. The war cost the Qing dynasty much of its wealth and stability.

name: The unification of Italy
text: In the 19th century a movement joined the many states of the Italian peninsula into one country. The revolutions of 1848 set the process going. In 1861 the states were joined to the Kingdom of Sardinia, and the Kingdom of Italy was made. The process was complete in 1871, when Rome became the capital. The movement is also called the Risorgimento.

name: The unification of Germany
text: The unification of Germany made the first nation-state of the Germans. It left out Austria. It began on 18 August 1866 with the North German Confederation, which the Kingdom of Prussia led. The south German states joined, and the German Empire, with 25 member states, was proclaimed on 18 January 1871.

name: British rule in India
text: From 1858 to 1947 the British Crown ruled the Indian subcontinent. This time is called the British Raj. It began after the Indian Rebellion of 1857, when rule passed from the East India Company to Queen Victoria. Britain ruled some areas directly; Indian rulers kept other areas, under British power. In 1947 the Raj was divided into two independent states, India and Pakistan.

name: The Meiji era in Japan
text: The Meiji era in Japan went from 1868 to 1912, the reign of Emperor Meiji. In this time Japan changed from an isolated feudal society, at risk of being colonised by Western powers, into a modern industrial country and a new great power. It took up Western ideas in science, technology, law and politics. Some former samurai rebelled against the fast changes in the 1870s.

name: The Scramble for Africa
text: In the late 19th and early 20th centuries, seven countries of western Europe invaded, conquered and colonised most of Africa. They were Belgium, France, Germany, Italy, Portugal, Spain and the United Kingdom. This is called the Scramble for Africa. From the start, nearly all the colonial governments said that they wanted to end slavery; that was a reason and also an excuse.

name: The Armenian genocide
text: The Armenian genocide was the planned destruction of the Armenian people in the Ottoman Empire during the First World War, from 1915 to 1917. The party that ruled the empire led it. About one million Armenians were murdered on death marches from Anatolia to the Syrian desert. Others, mostly women and children, were forced to become Muslims.

name: The Russian Revolution
text: The Russian Revolution began in 1917, in the middle of the First World War. Russia was short of bread and grain, and its army was losing. In March 1917 Tsar Nicholas II gave up the throne. In November 1917 the Bolsheviks, who promised peace, land and bread, took power by force in Petrograd. A civil war came after. In this time Russia ended its monarchy and took up a socialist government.

name: The Chinese Civil War
text: The Chinese Civil War was fought between the government of the Republic of China, led by the Kuomintang party, and the Chinese Communist Party. They fought, with breaks, from 1927 to 1949. From 1937 to 1945 the two sides mostly stopped, to fight the invasion by Japan. The Communists won mainland China and proclaimed the People's Republic of China in 1949. The other government went to Taiwan.

name: The Holodomor
text: The Holodomor was a famine in Soviet Ukraine from 1932 to 1933. It killed millions of Ukrainians. Scholars agree that people caused it, not nature. They do not agree on whether it was aimed at Ukrainians and whether it was a genocide. Some historians say that Joseph Stalin made the famine to end a Ukrainian independence movement. Others say that it came mostly from the change to collective farms.

name: Apartheid in South Africa
text: Apartheid was a system in South Africa, from 1948 to 1994, that kept people apart by race. The word means "separateness". The white people, who were the smaller part of the population, held the political, social and economic power. Laws put every South African in a racial group, and they separated homes, jobs and public places. One law made it illegal to marry a person of another race.

name: The end of colonial rule in Africa
text: Between the middle of the 1950s and 1976, the colonial governments in Africa came to an end, and independent countries took their place. These governments were set up in the Scramble for Africa. The change often came with violence, unrest and organised revolts. Among its main events were the Mau Mau rebellion, the Algerian War and the Congo Crisis.

name: The Vietnam War
text: The Vietnam War went from about 1955 to 30 April 1975. North Vietnam fought South Vietnam. China and the Soviet Union supported the North; the United States and other countries supported the South. Vietnam was divided in 1954, after France was defeated there. The United States sent many soldiers from 1965 and took the last out in 1973. In 1975 Vietnam, Laos and Cambodia all became communist.

name: The Cambodian genocide
text: From 1975 to 1979 the government of Cambodia, the Khmer Rouge under the dictator Pol Pot, persecuted and killed the country's own people. About 2 million people died, around a quarter of the population. The Khmer Rouge took power in April 1975. They emptied the cities and marched people to work camps in the country. Many were killed there; others died of forced work, hunger and disease.

name: The Atlantic slave trade
text: For 366 years, European slave traders forced about 12.5 million Africans onto ships that crossed the Atlantic Ocean. About 11 million lived through the voyage. In the Americas they were made to work as slaves, at first on sugar farms, and later on farms for other crops too.

name: Latter-day Saints (Mormons)
text: In 1830, in the west of New York, Joseph Smith founded what became The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. Its members became known as Mormons. They were driven out of Missouri in 1838. In 1846 their leader Brigham Young began to move about 15,000 of them west to the Great Basin, land that Mexico then held.

name: Ship lanes
text: Ships have kept records of the sea and the weather for hundreds of years. One large collection of these records goes from 1662 to today. At the detail level Full, this map uses such records to show the parts of the sea that many ships crossed, from 1750 on.

name: First World War
text: The First World War began in Europe in the summer of 1914. The Central Powers, among them Germany, Austria-Hungary and the Ottoman Empire, fought the Allies, among them France, Great Britain, Russia and Italy. In April 1917 the United States joined the war against Germany. The fighting stopped on November 11, 1918.

name: Second World War
text: Nazi Germany and Japan began the Second World War to rule Europe and Asia by force. In Europe the war began when Germany invaded Poland on September 1, 1939. Germany surrendered in May 1945, and Japan agreed to surrender on August 14, 1945. An estimated 55 million people died in the war.

name: The Holocaust
text: The Holocaust was the persecution and murder of six million Jews of Europe by Nazi Germany and those who helped it, between 1933 and 1945. Nazi Germany also persecuted and murdered millions of other people.

name: Cold War
text: The Cold War was the confrontation between the United States and the Soviet Union after the Second World War. A book of 1947 made the name well known. Both sides had nuclear weapons, and the threat of a nuclear war kept each side from more aggressive steps.

name: The civil war in Somalia
text: The civil war in Somalia grew out of resistance to the military government of Siad Barre in the 1980s. Armed groups that were based on clans brought down his government in 1991. After that, many armed groups fought for power, and Somalia had no central government. United Nations forces came in 1992 and left in 1995. The war was still going on in late 2026.

name: The civil war in Syria
text: The civil war in Syria began in March 2011. Many people protested against the government of Bashar al-Assad, and it answered with deadly force. Armed groups formed against it. Iran and Russia supported Assad; Qatar, Turkey, the United States and others armed his enemies. The Assad government fell in December 2024, after almost 14 years of war. Many sources see that as the end of the war.

name: The war in the Sahel
text: The war in the Sahel has gone on since 2012, with many sides. Most of it is in Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso. In 2012 Islamist Tuareg rebels overran Mali. By 2015 the war had spread to Burkina Faso and Niger, with heavy fighting and great need among the people. Later, anger at weak governments led to a series of coups. The war was still going on in late 2026.

name: The civil war in the Central African Republic
text: This civil war began when rebel groups called Séléka took several towns in 2012 and the capital in 2013. Militias called Anti-balaka fought them. Much of the tension is between Christian Anti-balaka and Muslim Séléka. There is also a struggle for diamonds and other resources. More than 1.1 million people fled their homes, of about 5 million. The war was still going on in late 2026.

name: The Ukraine war
text: The war between Russia and Ukraine began in February 2014. Russia occupied Crimea and annexed it from Ukraine, and it supported armed groups who started a war in the east of Ukraine. In February 2022 Russia began a full invasion of Ukraine. It is the largest conflict in Europe since the Second World War, with hundreds of thousands of deaths. The war was still going on in late 2026.

name: The civil war in Yemen
text: The civil war in Yemen began in September 2014, when Houthi forces took the capital, Sanaa, and then the government. Two sides each say that they are the government; the United Nations recognises one of them. In 2015 countries led by Saudi Arabia began air strikes. The Houthis hold Sanaa and most of the north. The war was still going on in late 2026.

name: The civil war in Myanmar
text: The civil war in Myanmar began after the army took power in a coup on 1 February 2021. Very many people protested, and the army answered with violence. Older fights between armed groups and the state grew much stronger. Hundreds of armed groups now fight across the country. The army's main opponents call for a democratic federal state. The war was still going on in late 2026.

name: The M23 war in eastern Congo
text: Since March 2022 the rebel group M23 has attacked in North Kivu, in the east of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Experts for the UN Security Council found that Rwanda gave M23 weapons. Rwanda and M23 say that Congo works with an armed group that is against Rwanda. In 2023 Human Rights Watch reported killings and other war crimes by M23. The war was still going on in late 2026.

name: The civil war in Sudan
text: Since April 2023 there has been a civil war in Sudan between the two main parts of the country's military government: the army, and a force called the Rapid Support Forces. The fighting began on 15 April 2023 in the capital, Khartoum, and then spread to the Darfur region. More than 14 million people have been forced from their homes. The war was still going on in late 2026.

name: The Gaza war
text: The Gaza war began on 7 October 2023, when the Palestinian armed group Hamas led an attack on Israel. It killed 1,195 people, and 251 were taken hostage. Israel then bombed and invaded the Gaza Strip. Over 74,000 Palestinians there have been killed. Many scholars and international bodies say that Israel's actions are genocide. Israel denies it. Fighting went on after a ceasefire of October 2025.

name: The Iran war
text: After the Twelve-Day War of June 2025, the United States and Israel have been at war with Iran and its allies since 28 February 2026. It began with hundreds of air strikes across Iran, which killed Iran's Supreme Leader, Ali Khamenei. Iran blocked trade through the Strait of Hormuz, and that caused a world fuel crisis. A ceasefire broke down on 8 July 2026. The war was still going on in late 2026.

name: Tiananmen Square protests and massacre, 1989
text: In April 1989 students began protests in Tiananmen Square in Beijing. They protested against corruption and rising prices, and they called for political and economic reforms. On the night of June 3 and 4 the army stormed the square with tanks and crushed the protests. The government of China said that over 200 people were killed. Western sources most often say hundreds or even thousands.

name: Persecution of the Uyghurs
text: The Uyghurs are a mostly Muslim people of Xinjiang, in the west of China. In 2022 the human rights office of the United Nations reported that serious human rights violations were committed against them and other mostly Muslim communities there. It said that the locking up of people since 2017, without a fair legal reason, may be crimes against humanity.
